parsed.attack: Perusall already is this product: line-anchored collaborative annotation of a set text, join links by class, peer notes surfaced before assessment, now with AI layered on, shipped and used at scale. Inside the school itself, Google Classroom with Docs comments and Microsoft's OneNote Class Notebook already provide free, roster-integrated, safeguarding-approved margin annotation that IT has already approved, and Seneca Learning owns the UK A-level free-tier student channel with class links and teacher assignment. For an under-18 audience whose channel is gated by school procurement, an incumbent already inside the building adding 'annotate your prescribed text as a class' is a small increment against distribution this product has to buy from scratch.
parsed.strongest_defence: School-owned tools are teacher-visible by design, which is exactly why candid student argument does not happen inside them; the product depends on an unsupervised peer space that Classroom and Class Notebook structurally cannot offer. Perusall's motion is institutional higher-education LMS sales rather than student-side freemium at A-level, and Seneca's model is publishing its own notes rather than hosting student-generated content.
parsed.verdict_reason: The mechanic exists as a shipped product and free school-issued equivalents already occupy the channel, leaving only the unsupervised-peer-space argument as genuine separation.
